title: The Last Interview on the List
名單上的最後一位面試者
paras: Dana Ortiz handled {{recruitment|recruitment}} for a small shipping company, and for two months she had been trying to fill a {{vacancy|vacancy}} on the dispatch team. On Tuesday afternoon she met the last {{applicant|applicant}} on her list, a quiet man named Victor Reyes.
戴娜．奧蒂茲替一家小型貨運公司負責招募，兩個月來一直想補上調度組的一個職缺。週二下午，她見了名單上的最後一位應徵者，一個安靜的男人，名叫維克多．雷耶斯。

His résumé listed his most recent {{occupation|occupation}} as senior dispatcher. The opening, however, was a {{junior|junior}} position with a modest salary. "Frankly, I'm worried you'll be bored," Dana said. Victor shrugged. "My old company closed in March. I'd rather start lower than not work at all."
他的履歷上寫著，他最近一份工作是資深調度員。然而這個缺是資淺職位，薪水不高。「老實說，我擔心你會覺得無聊。」戴娜說。維克多聳聳肩：「我之前的公司三月倒閉了。我寧可從低一點的職位做起，也不想沒工作。」

Dana was still {{reluctant|reluctant}} to say yes. Good people often leave a job like this within six months. Then Victor asked a question she hadn't expected. "As a {{prospective|prospective}} employee, may I ask who would train me? I'd like to learn your routes first, not change them." That answer settled it for her.
戴娜還是不太願意馬上點頭，因為像這樣的工作，好人才常常做不到半年就走了。接著維克多問了一個她沒料到的問題：「身為未來的員工，我可以問問誰會帶我嗎？我想先把你們的路線學起來，而不是急著去改它。」這個回答讓她下了決心。
On Thursday she {{formally|formally}} offered him the job by email. His {{acceptance|acceptance}} came back twenty minutes later, with one short line underneath: "When do I start?"
週四，她用電子郵件正式向他提出聘用。二十分鐘後，他的接受回覆就來了，底下只有短短一行：「我什麼時候開始上班？」
